text: For the choirmaster. Of David. In the LORD I have taken refuge. How can you say to me, "Flee to your mountain like a bird"?

versions.text: For the choirmaster. Of David. In the LORD I have taken refuge. How can you say to me, "Flee to your mountain like a bird!"?
versions.explanation: The stacked punctuation (!"?) is awkward in print and confusing for a reader aloud. A single question mark after the quotation is cleaner. (Optionally note in a footnote that the Hebrew reads "to my soul.")

text: For look, the wicked bend the bow; they fit their arrow to the string to shoot from the shadows at the upright in heart.
When the foundations are torn down, what can the righteous do?
The LORD is in his holy temple; the LORD's throne is in heaven. His eyes observe, his gaze examines the children of men.
The LORD tests the righteous, but the wicked and the one who loves violence—his soul hates them.

versions.text: The LORD tests the righteous, but the wicked and the one who loves violence his soul hates.
versions.explanation: As it stands the clause is hard to follow when read aloud; the object precedes the verb without any signal. A dash and an explicit pronoun keep the Hebrew word order's emphasis while making the sentence clear in oral reading.

text: On the wicked he will rain down snares, fire and sulfur and a scorching wind—the portion of their cup.
For the LORD is righteous; he loves righteous deeds. The upright will see his face.
